key_points: Reader job: a first-time studio owner can explain who supplies, reviews and approves each input. This is an educational objective (S1), not product evaluation.
Provide a clearly labelled invented example with a blank owner/due-date/status checklist; an illustrative sequence is not researched industry best practice.
Acceptance: the outline distinguishes client inputs from internal approval, and the closing action is to adapt the checklist to an actual project, not book a demo.
Evidence needed: a studio operator should review the sequence; no time-saved number, compliance claim, quote or mandatory legal step is established.
editorial.meta_description: A beginner-friendly sequence for design-studio onboarding: clarify scope, assign owners, collect inputs and agree the next handoff.
outline: H2: What onboarding should establish before delivery starts
H3: Distinguish scope agreement from collecting project inputs
H2: Stage 1 — agree the deliverable, approver and open questions
H2: Stage 2 — record required inputs, owners and due dates
H2: Stage 3 — confirm the handoff and route unresolved questions
H2: Use the checklist without assuming a software purchase
